title: 📰 AI news · October 31

items.title: Binance: $6.3 billion stolen through an engineer's laptop
items.text: Almost all of it left in 20 minutes: attackers used a compromised engineer's laptop to submit withdrawals in the exchange's name. Binance says no wallet private keys leaked. If you run a bot or service that moves money, one work computer with access can open everything. Check who has access to your payments and keys, and from which devices.

items.title: A fake Claude Code extension sat in Cursor's marketplace
items.text: The fake extension was available for 11 hours to up to 5,000 developers. It sent computer details to attackers and tried to set up a hidden SSH login. Editor extensions run on their own as soon as they load. Check your extension list and your SSH keys for entries you do not recognize. Free guide "Protecting your computer, code and access" — send the word "protect" to the bot.

items.title: A shared ChatGPT link could read private chats
items.text: Opening someone's link and clicking preview ran the attacker's code inside your account. OpenAI fixed it in eight days and found no real-world abuse. If you share chats with clients or a team, they may hold keys and data. Remove passwords and keys from shared chats.

items.title: A suspected spy board found inside a Trezor wallet
items.text: A buyer opened a Trezor Safe 5 and found an extra board with a cellular module. It could send the recovery phrase over a mobile network. If you keep money on a hardware wallet, it should come from the maker or an authorized seller. Check where yours was bought.

items.title: Open model GLM 5.3 built a Firefox exploit in 12 hours
items.text: Researchers asked the model to find a bug whose fix is visible in code but has not reached users yet. One exploit cost about $1,000. Mozilla fixed it in Firefox 159. If your browser has not been updated for a while, the fixes have not reached you. Update Firefox today.

items.title: A special SMS can knock out an Android phone
items.text: The flaw affects Android 12 and newer. Calls drop, and many messages make the phone unusable. A fix is in the October update for Android 14 and newer. If you run Android 14 or newer, install the October update.

items.title: A Claude Sonnet 5 agent operated on a mouse brain by itself
items.text: It chose a gene therapy out of 19 options, the brain region and the coordinates. A veterinarian approved every irreversible step. The results have not been independently verified.

items.title: OpenAI rewrote the behavior rules for its models
items.text: Five values anchor the rules: human intent, harm reduction, honesty, human agency and care. Agents get clearer rules on when they may act.

items.title: Gemini lets you edit the files it creates right in the chat
items.text: Documents, PDFs, slides, spreadsheets and code open full screen. No download needed. It is available to all Gemini users.

items.title: Google's first AI-chip satellite is online
items.text: The Suncatcher prototype carries four TPU chips. Gemma 4 on board wrote a haiku about space. Google plans two more such satellites in 2027.

items.title: Nokia 2360 Flip: a dual-screen flip phone with an SOS button
items.text: The SOS button calls a chosen contact and alerts up to five people. Family can change contacts and reminders remotely. The battery is removable, no price yet.

items.title: Samsung's Android XR glasses reportedly arrive in mid-December
items.text: Sales start in South Korea and the US. The glasses have no display, translate speech and last up to 9 hours. The price is not set.

takeaway: Today's news is about computers and extensions that give access to money and data. Recommendation: check which extensions your editor has and which devices can reach your keys and payments.
